from.place: set-of-representatives proof, affine case: a perfect object on Spec A comes from a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules

title: Perfect objects on an affine scheme are bounded finite projective complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme]. An object $E$ of $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ [def-pc-derived-category] is perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] if and only if $E$ is isomorphic in $D(\mathcal O_Y)$ to $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ for a bounded complex $P^\bullet$ of finite projective $A$-modules.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma perfect-lemma-perfect-affine (Tag 08EB), with More on Algebra, Definition 0656 (a perfect object of D(A) is one isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite projective A-modules)

proof.text: Use the affine derived equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] to write E as the object associated to a complex M of A-modules, i.e. E ≅ tilde(M) in D(O_Y) with M = RΓ(Y,E) in D(A).

source.place: Tag 08EB proof, reduction to the affine module description

proof.text: Forward implication. Assume E perfect. By [lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor], E is pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and every point of Y has an open neighbourhood U with integers a_U<=b_U such that H^i(E|_U ⊗^L G)=0 for all O_U-modules G and i outside [a_U,b_U]. Y=Spec(A) is quasi-compact, so finitely many such U cover Y; put a=min a_U, b=max b_U. For any O_Y-module G, (E⊗^L G)|_U = E|_U ⊗^L G|_U, and a sheaf zero on each member of an open cover is zero, so E has Tor amplitude in [a,b]. By [lem-pc-affine-tor-amplitude-criterion], M has Tor amplitude in [a,b]; by [lem-pc-affine-pseudo-coherent-criterion], M is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded-above complex of finite free, hence finite projective, A-modules. The ring criterion [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] gives a bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules with M ≅ P in D(A); applying the functor of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] gives E ≅ tilde(M) ≅ tilde(P) in D(O_Y).

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma 08EB proof: Lemmas 08E7 and 08E9, Cohomology Lemma 08CQ, More on Algebra Lemma 0658

proof.text: Conversely, if E is isomorphic to $\widetilde{P^\bullet}$ for a bounded complex P of finite projective A-modules, choose for each degree a finite free module A^{n_i} and an idempotent whose image is P^i. Applying the associated-sheaf functor gives each \widetilde{P^i} as a direct summand of \mathcal O_Y^{n_i}; the bounded complex \widetilde{P^\bullet} is therefore strictly perfect. The defining condition in [def-pc-perfect-complex] makes E perfect.
